nativeOutcome: One additional participant below the study's 3-item UCLA loneliness threshold at six months
decision: Publish an explicit, very-low-confidence decision estimate of approximately $14.9 million per 10 QALYs. This participant-level model is separate from the native six-month remission calculation. It starts with the native model's judgmental $1,040 cost per participant and 7% causal remission probability, then assigns each causal remission 50% of a systematic review's 0.04 annual lonely-versus-not-lonely health-utility gap for 0.5 effective year. That yields 0.0007 QALY per participant and approximately $14.9 million per better life. The conditional positive-effect range is approximately $1.25 million to $624 million; a true null, harm, or funding displacement remains plausible. This is a best-effort donor estimate, not a measured IOA effect, verified marginal price, rank, or funding recommendation.

sourceEvidence.friendshipLinePilot: The uncontrolled pilot enrolled 175 evaluation participants; 121 had any follow-up and 78 completed six months. Loneliness fell from 46% to 28%, but only 53% of scheduled calls were completed on average and the design does not identify a causal effect.
sourceEvidence.utilityReviewDesign: Systematic review of 19 observational studies reporting loneliness or social isolation alongside health-state utility values
sourceEvidence.utilityReviewPopulation: People with pre-existing health conditions; populations, conditions, loneliness measures, and utility instruments varied
sourceEvidence.utilityGapBasis: Two cross-sectional chronic-condition studies reported a 0.04 utility difference between lonely and not-lonely groups using HUI2 or EQ-5D-3L. The review could not pool estimates because of population, instrument, tariff, condition, and loneliness-measure heterogeneity.
sourceEvidence.interventionEvidence: A very-low-certainty friendly-visiting review did not establish a durable effect for a comparable service. Telephone RCTs show that structured behavioral activation or mindfulness can outperform telephone befriending, but those interventions, populations, doses, and comparators differ from Friendship Line.
sourceEvidence.boundary: No source maps IOA's 3-item UCLA threshold directly to health utility. The 0.04 gap is observational, binary, and confounded; the causal remission probability, transfer retention, and duration are MFI decision assumptions rather than study estimates.

modeledDonorCostPerParticipantUsd.basis: Bottom-up MFI synthesis of call dose, time, loaded resource cost, supervision, volunteer management, technology, training, and overhead. IOA does not publish Friendship Line program accounts or a current marginal price.

causalSixMonthRemissionProbability.basis: The midpoint attributes 7 percentage points of the uncontrolled 18-point decline to Friendship Line. The positive range is judgmental and reflects regression to the mean, secular change, selection, 45% six-month retention, and incomplete scheduled calls; null or harm remains outside the finite range.

retainedShareOfObservedUtilityGap.basis: The midpoint retains half of the cross-sectional 0.04 utility gap to reflect confounding, population transfer, instrument differences, and the absence of a validated 3-item UCLA threshold mapping. This is a judgment range, not a confidence interval.

effectiveDurationYears.basis: The midpoint combines gradual onset during the six-month program with limited persistence after the endpoint. The cautious case approximates a short-lived late gain; the optimistic case allows a full year. IOA measured neither onset nor post-program persistence.

modeledBridge.nullBoundary: The numeric range is conditional on a positive Friendship Line effect, a positive remission-to-utility relationship, and donor additionality. The pilot has no control group and only 78 of 175 baseline participants completed six months; the utility gap is observational; related telephone and befriending evidence does not identify IOA's effect; and IOA publishes no current marginal plan. If proactive calls have no causal loneliness effect, cause no health-utility gain, produce only transient change outside the assumed duration, harm some participants, or a private gift displaces health-plan or public funding, the impact price has no finite positive upper bound.

evidenceWeaknesses.label: Friendship Line causal effect
evidenceWeaknesses.why: The pilot had no concurrent comparison. Of 175 baseline participants, 121 had any follow-up, 78 completed six months, and an average 53% of scheduled calls were completed. The 7-point central causal remission probability is an MFI judgment; null or harm remains plausible.

evidenceWeaknesses.label: Remission-to-utility mapping
evidenceWeaknesses.why: No validated mapping was located from the 3-item UCLA threshold to a preference-based utility instrument. The binary 0.04 utility contrast is observational, heterogeneous, and drawn from chronic-condition populations.

evidenceWeaknesses.label: Timing and persistence
evidenceWeaknesses.why: The lower loneliness share at six months does not reveal onset, area under the utility curve, or persistence after the final interview. The 0.5-year midpoint is a decision assumption.

evidenceWeaknesses.label: Health-utility sensitivity
evidenceWeaknesses.why: The utility review warns that generic instruments may miss psychosocial change and that different instruments produce different values. IOA collected no preference-based utility measure.

evidenceWeaknesses.label: Marginal cost and funding room
evidenceWeaknesses.why: The $1,040 participant cost is built from MFI resource assumptions, not IOA accounts. Health-plan payment, public contracts, volunteer capacity, current cohort constraints, and displacement are unresolved.

excludedBenefits: Suicides averted, emergency visits, healthcare spending, mortality, and crisis resolutions not causally measured for Friendship Line
Depression, anxiety, unhealthy-day, referral, safety, and social-connection benefits not captured by the loneliness utility transfer
Caregiver, family, clinician, volunteer, and community spillovers
Benefits from inbound calls, grief groups, or other Institute on Aging programs
requiredEvidence: Pre-specify the 3-item UCLA outcome and causal estimand; use randomization or a credible concurrent comparison with complete participant flow, scheduled-call exposure, and missing-data analysis.
Collect a preference-based utility measure alongside loneliness at baseline, intermediate time points, six months, and post-program follow-up.

Publish Friendship Line program accounts, health-plan and public payments, volunteer and in-kind resources, current capacity constraints, displacement rules, and dated $100K, $1M, and $10M marginal plans.
